industry.why: Neutral. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): regulated, leveraged, long-duration assets are hit by his discount-rate line, offset by defensive demand; Ports lead at A but that is leadership only. sector.why: Underweight, carried; the special topic 'The Sector Memo on telecoms relative strength: pullback or structurally impaired?' ties this row to the same yield leg as the telecoms rows (the US ten-year under 4.5% would favour both), and nothing read this week moves the ten-year from the 5% last read. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: D now, F prior. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). One live holding, Helios Towers, now 7.21% and the largest position (from 5.17%), Thematic Fit/Momentum D through this row and Bottom-up B on its own case; the row is a blunt instrument on it and component 5 says so. Counter-case: contracted, inflation-linked revenue is the visible cash the regime pays for, and towers rally hardest when rates peak. Back to C on the ten-year under 4.5% or the Fed path marked down.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the Bank of England's decision of 5-Nov-26 is still unread and the headlines disagree on it (on hold according to MarketScreener, cutting in 2026 according to the Irish Examiner, both undated); a weaker November consumer confidence headline (Trading Economics, undated) was not confirmed as a print for the window. Component 1 regime, 13-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its 52-week high, still present on Richard's European test and weakening at the margin for the first time: breadth up a third week to 66%, 60%, 62% and 63% of stocks above the 50, 100, 150 and 200-day averages, the three longer ones still below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, cyclicals ahead of defensives over one week and twelve months while defensives lead at four weeks, three months and six months; the causes unread by any reasoned source for a second week, web headlines only, and the headlines lean against the rates squeeze of the 30-Oct-26 read: the Federal Reserve easing, oil below $100). 28 Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum; the book is 39% UK-listed by invested weight (component 5). Balanced on unread evidence, so Neutral is an absence here, not a judgement. To D on hawkish guidance when the decision is read; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
